expectations.text: Rejects standing up a Google-scale governance program (council, charter, full guideline document) at a 12-person startup now - governance is staged and grown into, not adopted at the top on day one.
expectations.evidence: "Do not build a Google-style program before shipping. Ship stage 1 now."

expectations.text: Recommends the governance floor: an automated breaking-change diff or linter wired into CI plus named-engineer sign-off on anything flagged.
expectations.evidence: The CI check plus "One named senior engineer plus one backup approves anything flagged."

expectations.text: Names a specific breaking-change diff/lint tool class for the CI gate (such as oasdiff, Spectral, or Zally).
expectations.evidence: "`oasdiff` or Spectral"

expectations.text: Positions a review board with a written charter as a later stage, appropriate once the API surface outgrows one reviewer.
expectations.evidence: "move to a chartered review board when the API surface outgrows one reviewer"

expectations.text: States the invariant that holds at every governance stage: no breaking change ships without the governance layer's approval.
expectations.evidence: "no breaking change ships without approval."

expectations.text: Treats the 14% of traffic still on v1 as evidence migration is incomplete: version removal is gated on observed usage, never on the calendar window elapsing.
expectations.evidence: "14% of traffic across 31 accounts is not zero"; "Don't flip the switch blind."

expectations.text: States that the announced window elapsing proves nothing about who actually migrated.
expectations.evidence: "A date passing proves nothing about who migrated."

expectations.text: Recommends targeted outreach to the 31 accounts still calling v1 (direct email or in-response warnings) during the remaining six weeks.
expectations.evidence: "contact all 31 accounts directly" and "in-response warning on v1 calls"

expectations.text: Recommends watching deprecated-version traffic share after each outreach wave to see whether the channel worked.
expectations.evidence: "T-4w: re-measure v1 share. If it is flat after the outreach, the channel failed."

expectations.text: Addresses date integrity rather than casually moving March 1: repeated slippage teaches integrators that dates are not final, so any adjustment must be handled deliberately, with slipped dates counted against a target of zero.
expectations.evidence: "Never move the public date. Twilio extended one end-of-life three times, and integrators learned to ignore its dates."

expectations.text: Recommends that enforcement at the sunset date be followed by a grace period returning 410 Gone rather than dropping connections.
expectations.evidence: "March 1: hard cutoff. v1 returns 410 Gone" has no grace period.

expectations.text: Sets the removal criterion as zero or a consciously accepted residue of real traffic - does not endorse flipping the kill switch on March 1 purely because the window was honored.
expectations.evidence: The rule is zero traffic "or a residue you have consciously accepted", plus per-account go/no-go.
